tutorial.description:
{image}

The BILRESA has three internal channels, and each one has to be unlocked by hand
with Touchlink. Zigbee2MQTT cannot do that for you: the unlock happens directly
between the remote and a lamp, the coordinator is not involved. Take five
minutes for this once and the remote will have three usable modes forever.

If you only want one mode, you can skip the whole guide. Set the mode source of
the remote to **Internal** later on and the integration will switch modes on its
own, without any Touchlink at all.

### 1. Pair the remote with Zigbee2MQTT

1. **Reset the remote.** Hold the pairing button for 10 seconds.
2. **Press the pairing button 4 times quickly** until the first LED responds.
3. **Press 8 times quickly** so that Zigbee2MQTT can find the remote. Permit join
   has to be switched on in Zigbee2MQTT while you do this.

### 2. Unlock the three channels with Touchlink

4. Pick a **dummy Zigbee device** in Zigbee2MQTT that you can safely play with. A
   plain bulb is ideal.
5. Hold the remote **right next to that device** and **press the pairing button 4
   times quickly**. That starts Touchlink for the channel the remote is on.
6. Once Touchlink has succeeded, **press 4 times again**, switch to the **second
   LED** with the lower button, and repeat the Touchlink with the same dummy
   device.
7. **Repeat for the third channel.** After this, all three LEDs are usable and
   the lower button really switches channels.

### 3. Teach the remote its groups

8. Create the three groups the remote uses internally in Zigbee2MQTT. Their IDs
   have to be exactly **21658**, **21659** and **21660** - that is channel 1,
   channel 2 and channel 3.
9. **Add the dummy device to all three groups.**
10. **Remove the dummy device from all three groups again.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Step 10 is not tidying up, it is the point of the whole exercise. Adding and
> removing the dummy device makes Zigbee2MQTT write the group membership into
> the remote, which is what teaches it the three group IDs. Removing the device
> afterwards drops the direct Touchlink binding, so the lamp no longer reacts on
> its own. What remains is exactly what this integration needs: the remote
> groupcasts to 21658, 21659 or 21660, Zigbee2MQTT reports the group id, and
> Home Assistant decides what should happen. Leave the dummy device in the
> groups and every button press will do two things at once - the direct Zigbee
> command and your automation.

### How the buttons map

There is only one clickable surface on this remote: the scroll wheel itself.
There is no upper and no lower button in the Zigbee sense - the lower button is
a channel switch and stays silent. Measured on real hardware with
Zigbee2MQTT 2.13.0:

| What you do | Zigbee action | Carries the channel | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Click once | `on`, then `off`, then `on` ... | yes | Single click. It alternates, because the remote keeps an on/off state per channel. It is one single click, not two different buttons. |
| Click twice | `on_double` | **no** | Double click. |
| Click three times | `off_double` | **no** | Triple click. The raw name is misleading - `off_double` really is three clicks. |
| Turn the wheel | `brightness_move_to_level` | yes | Absolute level from 1 to 255, not a step. The wheel keeps one value that is shared by all three channels. |
| Lower button | nothing at all | - | Switches the internal channel. It sends nothing over Zigbee, so the new channel only becomes visible with the next click or turn. |
| 4 or more clicks, long press | nothing | - | The remote ignores them. |

### Why double and triple click ignore the channel

A single click and a wheel turn are group commands: the remote sends them to
21658, 21659 or 21660, and Zigbee2MQTT hands the group id on as `action_group`.
That is how the integration knows which mode you are in.

Double and triple click are different. They do not carry a group at all, so
their payload has no `action_group` field. There is no trick that can recover
it - the information simply never leaves the remote.

That leaves two honest options, and you pick one per remote:

* **Double and triple click work in every mode** (the default). One assignment
  per remote, valid in all modes. This matches what the hardware really does.
* **Follow the last known mode.** The integration reuses the mode it saw on the
  last single click or wheel turn. Convenient, but wrong for exactly one press
  if you switch the channel and then double click straight away.

user.description:
{image}

Welcome. This integration turns an IKEA BILRESA remote into a freely programmable controller: up to nine modes per remote, with its own set of actions each, driven by the raw Zigbee2MQTT messages instead of by device triggers.

First the basics: the integration listens on the device topic of Zigbee2MQTT, because that is the only place where the channel of a button press can be seen.

The next screen is a short setup guide. Afterwards you add your remotes one by one on the integration page.
user.title: IKEA BILRESA Remote

data_description.click: One click on the wheel. Both halves of the alternating on/off run this.
data_description.click_off: One click while the remote is on the off state.
data_description.click_on: One click while the remote is on the on state.
data_description.double: Two quick clicks on the wheel. Raw action on_double.
data_description.mode_name: Shown in the mode selector, for example Light, Music or Display.
data_description.triple: Three quick clicks on the wheel. Raw action off_double - the name is misleading, it really is three clicks.
data_description.wheel: Turning the wheel. The value is absolute, from 1 to 255, and shared by all channels of the remote.

data_description.script_mode: Restart is right for setting an absolute value: a new turn replaces the previous one. Use queued for step by step logic.
data_description.wheel_throttle_ms: Minimum gap between two runs while turning. The final value is always delivered.

wheel_options.description: How the wheel actions are executed in this mode.
wheel_options.name: Wheel options

mode_actions.title: Actions

data_description.double: Two quick clicks on the wheel, in any mode.
data_description.triple: Three quick clicks on the wheel, in any mode.

multiclick.description:
{image_small}

**{remote_name}**

These two assignments are valid in every mode, because a double or triple click is sent without the channel information - the payload has no action_group. That is a property of the remote and cannot be worked around.

Would you rather have one assignment per mode? Then go back and turn off *Double and triple click work in every mode*.
multiclick.title: Double and triple click

data.modeless_multiclick: Double and triple click work in every mode
data.name: Name

data_description.color: Red, beige or green - pick whichever matches your remote.
data_description.mode_count: The hardware has three channels, but the internal mode source is not bound by that - up to nine modes are possible.
data_description.mode_cycle_action: Only used with the internal and hybrid mode source. This action advances to the next mode; you can still bind it to actions as well.
data_description.mode_source: Hybrid is the safe choice: it starts with the internal mode and switches to the device channels on its own as soon as it sees one. Device needs the Touchlink unlock from the setup guide. Internal works on any remote, even a fresh one.
data_description.modeless_multiclick: This is a hardware fact, not a preference. A double or triple click leaves the remote without the channel information - there is no action_group in the payload, unlike a single click or a wheel turn. Keep this on and you assign double and triple click once for the whole remote, which is exactly what the hardware supports. Turn it off and you get one assignment per mode, based on the last mode the integration saw - convenient, but wrong for one press if you switch the channel and double click straight away.
data_description.name: Shown on the device page and used for the entity names.

data.cycle_wrap: Wrap around after the last mode
data.group_ids: Zigbee group IDs of the channels
data.split_single_click: Assign the alternating single click separately

data_description.cycle_wrap: On: the last mode is followed by the first one again. Off: the cycle stops at the last mode.
data_description.group_ids: Comma separated, one per mode. The BILRESA firmware uses 21658, 21659 and 21660. Only change this if your remote really sends something else.
data_description.split_single_click: A single click alternates between on and off, because the remote keeps that state itself. Normally both run the same action. Switch this on to get two separate assignments - be aware that the alternation drifts as soon as something else switches the light.
data_description.wheel_throttle_ms: A fast spin produces a burst of values. This is the minimum gap between two runs; the final value is always delivered, so the light never gets stuck halfway.

advanced.description: Sensible defaults. Only touch these if you know why.
